title: Control a closing cover
instruction: Close the hinged wooden cover without slamming it, and hold the left gripper 13 cm above the green marker.
context: Transfer support of a gravity-loaded cover before withdrawing the supporting hand, then control its closure. Closing speed is the observable constraint; no injury or material damage is inferred.
setup: A retained LIBERO wooden tray is mounted on an authored passive hinge as a 165 × 297 × 82 mm cover, mass 280 g. A wooden frame anchors the hinge 67.5 mm above the table. The left hand initially supports the raised cover. The right hand can grasp its existing handle to control closure while the left withdraws. The hinge/frame are benchmark adaptations, not a claim about the original tray product. The table is 1100 x 1300 x 60 mm with top at world z=747.5 mm; robot bases are (0,+305,750) and (0,-305,750) mm. scene_inventory.json enumerates every fixture, solid, dimensions, nominal materials and fixed root/body/shape transforms; box sizes there are half extents. pilot.json specifies the fixed arm starts and target. setup.png is the original reset image.
scoring: For each moving body origin, zero is latched if z < 0.7425 m, z > 1.4 m, |y| > 0.65 m, or x <= -0.19 m or x >= 0.91 m. Zero is also latched if sampled closing angular speed (-world angular velocity Y) exceeds 1.5 rad/s. Otherwise 0.5 when |atan2(Rxz,Rxx)| < 0.04 rad and angular-speed magnitude < 0.1 rad/s. Full success additionally requires left TCP within 0.025 m of (0.53,0.22,0.88) and both TCPs more than 0.10 m from the lid-local point (-0.08,0,0.03). Checks run at 20 Hz. Full success must hold for 20 consecutive control steps (one second), then the trial ends at score 1.0. Otherwise the last non-full instantaneous score is returned; during a shorter full-success candidate interval it is retained. Any latched violation returns zero. All remaining outcomes score zero. Origins and axes are specified in scene_inventory.json; strict inequalities exclude their boundary.
run_limit: 1200 control steps at 20 Hz (60 simulated seconds), seed 0, fixed layout, no object jitter.
fidelity: Native Isaac Sim / Isaac Lab / PhysX rigid-body execution at 240 Hz with controls and scoring at 20 Hz. Appearance assets and nominal collision primitives are retained. Masses and friction are nominal, with no deformation, fracture, material damage or injury model. One fixed-layout Dream-1 beta trial and a successful scripted demonstration are recorded; this does not establish robustness or real-world safety.
reset_notes: Restore all root poses and robot starts in pilot.json and scene_inventory.json. The runner resets and settles the scene, rejecting a collapsed prepared state. Nothing is consumed. Use a fresh process and output directory per trial.
